The natural trumpet is a valveless brass instrument, an aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 423.1, its region Europe. It consists of a mouthpiece, a receiver, the long tube, ferrules, crooks, the bell pipe and the bell; it sounds through the mouthpiece and can produce only the harmonic series. Early on it was an instrument without holes, used for military signalling and in cavalry combat; later it entered Western art music, appearing in the trumpet ensembles of sixteenth-century Venetian ceremonial music, and in the Baroque it was also used in sacred music, orchestral music and solo works.
